snippet.title: Unpopular opinion: you don't need to ask ChatGPT everything
snippet.description:
This might be an unpopular opinion, but most people don't need to use cloud AI models for everything.

Most people are using the most state-of-the-art AI models from ChatGPT or Claude to summarize documents or write emails for them, and frankly these models have gotten too smart for that. You don't need all the compute for everyday tasks. 

Running local models directly on your computer means you don't need the internet, your data is completely private, and you're not at the whims of the big AI labs. 

With amazing new local models and even better hardware, your computer can handle 90% of the simple things we ask AI to do.

Would you switch to using a local AI model?

snippet.title: The Wildest Things People Vibe Coded With Fable 5
snippet.description:
I messed up. 

Everyone has been talking about the drama that went down around Claude Fable and Mythos getting shut down, including myself. But I got distracted from the REAL story here, which is just how crazy good these models were and the amazing things people were able to build with them.  

These are just a few examples, but it's insane that people built full scale projects and business ideas and NONE of them were engineers with massive dev budgets. They were just regular people with a good idea. 

What used to require a full development team and months of work now takes a single afternoon and a good AI model. We are watching in real time a massive shift in WHO gets to build things. 

But of course, the party was cut short because Anthropic was ordered to suspend foreign access to Fable 5 over security concerns, literally describing their own tech as "too powerful." 

And I get why that sounds terrifying. But look at what people actually did with it in the short window they had: they solved problems, built businesses, and created cool things to share with the world. That’s what happens when you put genuinely useful tech into the hands of the people. 

#Claude #Anthropic #AI #Entrepreneurship #vibecoding

Marcus walks through what actually changed in the Fable 5 redeployment, why a Pentagon undersecretary negotiated guardrail terms with Anthropic's CEO by email, and what it means for builders who assume they're getting the model they paid for.

In this episode:

03:47 Meituan 1T open model — Meituan open-sources a trillion-parameter MIT-licensed model trained without NVIDIA, while Microsoft bets $2.5B and 6,000 employees on enterprise AI

snippet.title: Why AGI Is Close but Not Here Yet | Ray Kurzweil | MOONSHOTS
snippet.description:
In 1999, Ray Kurzweil predicted human-level AI by 2029. Stanford's top AI experts said 100 years. Three years from the deadline, he says two things are still missing: AI that understands physics, and a robot that knows the difference between what goes in the fridge and what goes in the trash.

- LLMs went from unremarkable to world-changing in 12 months. AI now outperforms human doctors at diagnosis by 50%.

- LLMs have only been truly effective for six months, according to Ray. A year ago, "not really all that impressive."

- The Genome Project was 1% done at the halfway mark. One doubling later — done. We're at that same moment with AGI. 

- Software alone has improved roughly a millionfold over 70 years. Total compute gain = hardware (75,000 trillion fold) × software (million fold).
